bull_argument.argument:
Gamuda's construction earnings grew 19% at a stable 5% segment margin, while a RM61.2bn order book supplies work to convert into future profit. CFO improved to RM807.6m from an outflow. Those observed improvements, together with a constructive price trend and supportive investment backdrop, make continued construction execution a plausible source of upside.

The valuation already anticipates improvement: 29.35x trailing earnings is demanding against 5% group profit growth. Net debt is RM9.414bn, gearing 72%, and RM3.401bn investing outflow depended on financing. The bull case therefore requires collections to follow construction profit and property weakness to ease; management's sub-70% gearing target is not delivered deleveraging. Existing positive CFO offers a starting point, but does not establish that the expansion is self-funding.
key_points: Construction growth, stable segment margin and backlog support execution upside.
CFO turned positive, providing a measurable collection starting point.
Premium trailing valuation and 72% gearing require stronger cash conversion.

bear_argument.argument:
Gamuda's 19% construction-profit growth and improved CFO are substantive, but group profit grew only 5% at 29.35x trailing earnings. Property profit fell 18%, gearing rose from 53% to 72%, and short-term borrowing increased to RM6.341bn from RM2.906bn. Those measured changes raise funding and rollover sensitivity despite a profitable backlog.

RM807.6m CFO did not match RM3.401bn investing outflow; RM3.389bn financing inflow supports the bull's admission that expansion is not self-funding. The RM61.2bn order book can generate value only with funded collections and execution. Management's late-FY27 gearing target is a prospective repair plan. The constructive trend does not offset current financing dependence or establish returns high enough to justify the growth-priced valuation.
key_points: Gearing and short-term borrowing increased substantially.
Valuation anticipates stronger group conversion than observed.
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: Construction profit growth is the bull's strongest evidence, but collections have not funded the broader investment program: RM807.6m CFO versus RM3.401bn investing outflow. A future gearing target does not repair that observed dependence.

bull_argument.argument:
The bear correctly distinguishes positive CFO from a self-funded investment program. Yet construction profit increased 19% at a stable 5% segment margin, and CFO moved from negative RM78.5m to positive RM807.6m. These are actual improvements in execution and collections, rather than proof resting solely on RM61.2bn of orders.

The investment outflow and rising short-term debt require caution, especially at 29.35x trailing earnings. The upside scenario is further construction conversion and property repair reducing the financing dependence; management's sub-70% gearing aim is a testable target, not delivered relief. A constructive trend supports interest without funding projects. The strongest bullish case therefore rests on an improving operating engine that can service a larger book, while conceding that current investment scale still makes a purchase highly conditional.
key_points: Construction profitability and collections improved in observed results.
Investing cash outflow is not automatically recurring capex or FCF.
Gearing repair depends on delivery rather than a management promise.
bull_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: RM807.6m CFO does not fund RM3.401bn investing outflow, as the bear says. But the move from negative CFO and 19% construction-profit growth show real conversion progress, preserving upside if further collections and property improvement reduce dependence. I do not treat the target as current deleveraging.

bear_argument.argument:
The bull's construction profit growth of 19% at a stable 5% margin and CFO turnaround demonstrate real execution progress. They answer a backlog-only thesis objection. The scale remains important: RM807.6m CFO accompanied RM3.401bn investing outflow and RM3.389bn financing inflow, while gearing rose from 53% to 72%.

Short-term borrowing increased to RM6.341bn from RM2.906bn, adding rollover sensitivity; property profit fell 18%. At 29.35x trailing earnings against 5% group profit growth, the price relies on meaningful further improvement. The RM61.2bn book can support that scenario, but financing and collection burdens are already observable. Management's gearing target supplies a repair objective rather than achieved relief. The bull establishes a better engine, yet current expansion still increases risk faster than demonstrated group earnings compensation.
key_points: Investment remains externally funded and gearing rose.
The valuation requires improvement beyond current group growth.
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers whether execution has improved, not whether that improvement offsets the increased funding burden. I accept positive CFO while retaining leverage, rollover and growth-priced valuation as concrete reasons against aggressive entry.

bull_case_summary: Gamuda has 19% construction-profit growth at stable segment margin and a CFO turnaround to RM807.6m. Round two uses actual execution and collections rather than backlog alone to defend conditional upside from the RM61.2bn book.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts progress but notes RM3.401bn investing outflow, RM3.389bn financing inflow and gearing rising to 72%. Short-term borrowing of RM6.341bn and only 5% group profit growth leave substantial further improvement priced into 29.35x earnings.
key_points_of_agreement: The investment program remains externally funded.
Management gearing targets are prospective and investing outflow is not automatically FCF.
key_points_of_disagreement: Whether improving construction economics compensate the larger funding and rollover burden at a growth-priced valuation.
unresolved_uncertainties: Further collections, property recovery and delivered gearing reduction.
Sustainable return on funded expansion and rollover requirements.
